messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Spanish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Spanish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
así mi alma, que aún huía, se volvió atrás para volver a mirar el paso que nunca dejó jamás una persona viva.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|--------------------|------------------|--------| | così | resultative adverb “so” | así | so | OK | | l'animo | noun “the soul” | alma | soul | OK | | mio | possessive adjective “my” | mi | my | OK | | ch'ancor | relative pronoun + adverb “which still” | que aún | which still | OK | | fuggiva | imperfect verb “was fleeing” | huía | was fleeing | OK | | si | reflexive clitic | se | (reflexive) | OK | | volse | passato remoto “turned” | volvió | turned | OK | | a *(first)* | preposition introducing direction “to” (in *a retro*) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | retro | noun used adverbially “back” | atrás | back | OK | | a *(second)* | preposition introducing infinitive purpose “to” | para | for / to | OK | | rimirar | infinitive “to look again” | volver a mirar | to look again | OK | | lo | definite article “the” | el | the | OK | | passo | noun “pass” | paso | pass | OK | | che | relative pronoun “which” | que | which | OK | | non | negation particle “never” | nunca | never | OK | | lasciò | passato remoto “left” | dejó | left | OK | | già | adverb “already” | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | mai | adverb “never” | jamás | never | OK | | persona | noun “person” | persona | person | OK | | viva | adjective “living” | viva | living | OK |
### Items flagged
- **UNNECESSARY**: - `a` (first) – the directional preposition is absorbed into the adverb *atrás* in Spanish, so the separate preposition is not needed. - `già` – the sense of “already” is already conveyed by the emphatic negation *jamás*; a separate word is unnecessary.
No source words are missing, wrong, or grammatically mismatched.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Spanish script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Spanish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 26: - Original: **se volvió atrás para volver a mirar el paso** - Issue: none - Corrected: **se volvió atrás para volver a mirar el paso**
